# Grid header text overflows into the next header instead of clipping

## Context

A grid header whose label is wider than its column paints over the header to its right. The case was a grid with composed labels at default widths: "observed · Throughput" ran into the next header, "queued · Pulse", and both became unreadable. It was captured as defect-note `9f87f40d6a38a7ce`. @neo-opus-grace confirmed the cause in source during a design read and asked for this promotion.

## The Problem

Composed labels (key · field) and narrow columns hit this first, but any `text` longer than its `width` does. The label isn't cut off: it keeps painting into the neighbour, so neither header can be read. Content-sized cells already handle the same situation with a one-line ellipsis; headers have no equivalent.

## The Architectural Reality

- `resources/scss/src/grid/header/Button.scss` l.1–20: `.neo-grid-header-button` is a flex row with `flex-shrink: 0` and `white-space: nowrap`, and no overflow rule.
- The label is `.neo-button-text` (`src/button/Base.mjs:170`). Its rule in the header (`Button.scss` l.130–145) sets colour and font only.
- Clipping the whole button would also cut the sort glyph and the menu trigger, which are siblings of the label.
- Only the menu-wrapper variant shrinks: `.neo-grid-menu-wrapper > .neo-grid-header-button` gets `min-width: 0` (l.156).
- Precedent: fixed-height tree cells keep a one-line ellipsis (`src/grid/column/Tree.mjs:25`, `resources/scss/src/grid/column/component/Tree.scss:45`).

Design authority: none found (searched: `src/grid`, `src/button`, `resources/scss/src/grid`, `resources/scss/src/button` and `learn/guides` for "ellipsis" and "overflow"). The fork sits on the owning record, the header-button block in `Button.scss`: overflow, as today, or a one-line ellipsis on the label, as proposed. The PR records the chosen intent there in one comment line.

## The Fix

In `resources/scss/src/grid/header/Button.scss`:
- Give the header's `.neo-button-text` `overflow: hidden`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, `white-space: nowrap` and `min-width: 0`, so a long label ends in an ellipsis inside its own column.
- Make the flex chain allow it, so the label can shrink while the sort glyph keeps its size.
- One comment line above the rule states the intent: a header label clips like a fixed-height tree cell.

The label stays in the DOM, so the column header's accessible name is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A header whose `text` is wider than its column ends in an ellipsis inside that column, and the neighbouring header is untouched.
- [ ] A clipped header keeps its sort indicator fully visible.
- [ ] Headers that fit render as before: no ellipsis, same width.
- [ ] Evidence: a before/after frame of a grid with two long, narrow headers, e.g. `columns: [{dataField: 'a', text: 'observed · Throughput', width: 110}, {dataField: 'b', text: 'queued · Pulse', width: 110}]`.

## Out of Scope

- Header bands, i.e. grouped headers (#20379, PR #20397, which doesn't touch `Button.scss`).
- Sizing columns to their header text.
- A tooltip carrying the full label.

## Related

#20379 / #20397 (header groups), #19562 (header font size in narrow windows, same file), defect-note `9f87f40d6a38a7ce`.
